svg.title: Home-made LSP: opening a channel and receiving over Lightning
svg.text: Home-made LSP: opening a channel and receiving over Lightning

g.text: app LN node, no channels yet
"pnpm -F wallet lsp fund": the payer wallet sends sats to node A, which then creates colored UTXOs: rgb-lib funds RGB
The LSP answers with pubkey, host, peerPort, asset ID and whether it has liquidity available. The app now knows who to
The app connects as a peer
connectPeer on pubkey@host:9735 (Lightning P2P network). The LSP refuses requests from nodes that are not connected
The LSP answers 202 "opening". If it is still preparing funds it answers 503 and the app retries every minute (max 10
30,010 sats of capacity, 10 TUSDT on the LSP side, 3.1M msat initial push, private channel with anchors. One fixed
The asset data for the channel goes through the RGB proxy.
The tx enters Mutinynet. One block (~30 s) is needed before the channel is usable.
From here the app can receive TUSDT over Lightning with no further on-chain transactions.
The app checks the status: "open". The Lightning panel shows the channel.
A customer pays the app: HTLC to the LSP
The customer has no channel with us, but has one with the LSP: the payment goes through there.
The LSP forwards into the private channel
forwardToPrivateChannels is on (channels to app nodes are private). The TUSDT reach the app within seconds.
The LSP forwards into the private channel
forwardToPrivateChannels is on (channels to app nodes are private). The TUSDT reach the app within seconds.
